answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so voting influence depends on paths from anchored attestations, not merely on declared identities. A Sybil cluster may wander internally, but a sparse external cut gives it low conductance: few walk transitions carry probability mass across its boundary. Under a degree-balanced walk, this bounds the cluster’s reachable voting mass; a marble of mutually endorsing accounts cannot gain weight through a hollow boundary.
